nodes.summary: `max_b ∑_{j ≠ i} v j b`, the best welfare the other agents could get without agent `i` (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.19).
nodes.title: Clarke pivot term

nodes.summary: If `f v` maximizes the welfare at `v` and all valuations are nonnegative, then with Clarke pivot payments every agent reporting truthfully gets a nonnegative utility (Nisan 2007, Lemma 9.20, second part).
nodes.title: Individual rationality

nodes.summary: For nonnegative bids and a winner rule `w` that picks a highest bid, the Clarke pivot payment of the VCG mechanism on single-item valuations is the second-price payment (Nisan 2007, §9.3.5.1).
nodes.title: The second-price auction is the VCG mechanism with Clarke pivot payments

nodes.summary: If the pivot terms do not depend on the agents' own reports and `f v` has at least the welfare (at the true profile `v`) of the alternative chosen after agent `i` reports `w`, then agent `i` does not gain by reporting `w` instead of `v i`.
nodes.title: VCG truthfulness, pointwise

nodes.summary: The payment `h i v - ∑_{j ≠ i} v j (f v)` of agent `i` in the VCG mechanism with alternative rule `f` and pivot terms `h` (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.16).
nodes.title: Groves payment

nodes.summary: Each `h i` depends only on `v₋ᵢ`.
nodes.title: Pivot terms independent of the own report

nodes.summary: VCG with Clarke pivot payments is incentive compatible.
nodes.title: VCG with Clarke pivot payments is incentive compatible

nodes.summary: A mechanism that chooses a welfare-maximizing alternative for every reported profile and charges Groves payments with pivot terms that do not depend on the agents' own reports is incentive compatible (Nisan 2007, Theorem 9.17).
nodes.title: Vickrey–Clarke–Groves theorem

nodes.summary: The direct mechanism `(f, p)` is incentive compatible: for every agent `i`, every profile `v` and every report `w` of agent `i`, `v i (f v) - p v i ≥ v i (f v') - p v' i` with `v' = update v i w` (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.15).
nodes.title: Incentive compatibility (quasi-linear, dominant strategies)

nodes.summary: With at least two agents, the agents other than `i` form a nonempty set.
nodes.title: Some other agent exists

nodes.summary: With single-item valuations, the others' welfare is `0` when agent `i` wins and the winner's bid otherwise.
nodes.title: Others' welfare of a winner

nodes.summary: The welfare of the agents other than `i` does not depend on agent `i`'s valuation.
nodes.title: The others' welfare ignores the own valuation

nodes.summary: The total value `∑_{j ≠ i} v j a` of the alternative `a` for the agents other than `i`.
nodes.title: Welfare of the others

nodes.summary: In the auction with winner rule `w`, the winner pays the highest competing bid `max_{j ≠ i} t j` and losers pay nothing (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.12).
nodes.title: Second-price payment

nodes.summary: In the second-price auction with a winner rule `w` that picks a highest bid, no bidder gains by bidding `s` instead of its value `t i`, whatever the other nonnegative bids: its utility `t i - (price)` if it wins, `0` otherwise, is largest when it bids its value (Vickrey 1961, through Nisan 2007, Proposition 9.13). The statement is for nonnegative values and bids, the valuation domain of Nisan 2007, §9.3.5.1, and is…

nodes.summary: The alternatives are the possible winners `a : ι` of one item, and the bids `t` give agent `i` the value `t i` if it wins and `0` otherwise (Nisan 2007, §9.3.1 and §9.3.5.1).

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
